correctness.rationale: For general P7 the rank-four intersection is a smooth curve avoiding rank-two forms; local block Pfaffian gives a nondegenerate six-variable quadratic and reduced Jacobian scheme. The projective-bundle resolution has canonical class \(-6\xi-5c_1(Q)\); Pfaffian trivialization gives \(c_1(Q)=2\xi\) on the curve, hence \(\omega_C=\mathcal O_C(4)\). Exact Schubert coefficient evaluation gives degree 84 (also the Harris–Tu degeneracy degree); genus follows as 169. Morse–Bott vanishing cycles supply Euler defect 336. The extracted exact-integer checker confirms 84, 168, 24024, 169, 1648, 1312. Genericity and local analytic claims are proven geometrically, not inferred from finite experiments.

originality.rationale: The first-public September 18 Fano paper motivates the adjacent P6 Pfaffian model; its accessible abstract does not give the proposed P7 singular-curve genus/canonical/Euler determination. Iliev–Markushevich pp. 1-3 and 7-9 establish the universal rank stratification and P4 smoothness, not the P7 invariants. Harris–Tu gives the universal degree, so degree 84 alone is not new. value.rationale: The genus and intrinsic canonical polarization of the first positive-dimensional singular locus of a natural general Pfaffian quartic, together with the exact transverse type, give a motivated geometric package beyond the classical degree count. The Euler defect 336 quantitatively controls smoothing topology of a rational quartic sixfold studied through Grassmannian/Pfaffian correspondences. This is a substantive complete natural invariant, not an arbitrary slice, routine parameter substitution, or a claimed general conjecture solution.
